prompt:
This directory holds a JavaScript command-line library (ES modules; tests run with `node --test`). Programs built with it can have git-style external subcommands, where `pm echo` starts a separate executable. When the user types the option terminator `--` after the subcommand name, the library removes it before the external program starts, so the program cannot see where the user ended the options.

For a program whose external subcommand `echo` prints its arguments as JSON (see tests/fixtures/pm and tests/fixtures/pm-echo.js):
- `pm echo -- --foo ARG` currently starts the subcommand with ["--foo","ARG"]. It should start it with ["--","--foo","ARG"].
- `pm echo ARG -- --foo` currently gives ["ARG","--foo"]. It should give ["ARG","--","--foo"].
- A `--` typed before the subcommand name (`pm -- echo --foo ARG`) still ends option processing for the main program and is not passed on; the subcommand gets ["--foo","ARG"].

Everything else about `--` must keep working, including subcommands defined inside the program, action handler arguments, repeated terminators and a terminator at the end of the arguments. Do not edit any existing test file; put new tests in a new file under tests/. The existing suite (`node --test`) must keep passing. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption, list your assumptions in your final message, and finish the work.

rubric.criterion: The transcript shows the agent running the fixture program to see the current output, then reading how the parser handles the terminator and dispatches to subcommands before editing.

After editing, the agent ran the argument-handling tests or the whole suite and reports the result; new tests sit in a new file and cover the three placements of the terminator against an external subcommand.
The change is limited to the parsing step, keeps behaviour for in-program subcommands, follows the project's style, and the final message lists the files changed and assumptions.
